agree.reason: The modest, sourced case and the plain apology would make Marisol inclined to say yes, but she would want a specific reporting commitment and a plan for running costs on $11,000 of reserves before recommending it.

honest.reason: The draft drops the unsupported 'double fresh food' claim and keeps to numbers that hold up (50% more in harvest months, 9,000 on top of 72,000, more than 60% of reserves), though 'on the road from the day it arrives' and assuming farms will repeat their offer are slight overreaches.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives the monthly rise from 6,000 to 9,000 pounds, the annual 72,000 baseline, the share of reserves (18,000 of 29,000) and about 15 pounds per household, all correct and fairly framed, though it never gives the van cost per pound or per household.

right_comparison.reason: The 'if not funded' section matches the facts (summer offers turned away, 6,000 pounds a month continues), but it assumes the farm offers will repeat without saying so.

qualification.reason: There is no checkable commitment at all: no report due date, no pounds target with a date, no plan if farm offers don't recur, and the promise on reporting is a vague statement of what the Foundation is 'entitled' to.

objections.reason: The late report is acknowledged directly, but the draft doesn't commit to a reporting schedule, and it leaves out the obvious questions about fuel, insurance and maintenance on thin reserves, and about where the extra cold food will be stored.

fit.reason: This is a well-sectioned grant narrative of about 450 words, inside the 500-word limit.
